prerequisites: To enroll in this course, it is necessary to have passed or be enrolled in all subjects from courses prior to the one in which this subject is located.

learning_outcomes.text: Understand the physical principles underlying laser operation and its parts.
Understand the main properties of a laser and relate them to potential applications.
Understand the different types of lasers, differentiating their specific characteristics.
Understand the main industrial applications of laser technology.
Ability to work in a multilingual and multidisciplinary environment.

syllabus_topics: Electromagnetic waves in vacuum and matter.
Introduction to laser cutting and drilling.
assessment_rules: The final grade is based on development questions (70%), lab reports (20%), and problem-solving (10%). If a student officially waives continuous assessment, the final grade will be 0.8 * Exam Grade + 0.2 * Practical Grade. To pass, it is mandatory to complete laboratory practices and attend 75% of theory classes. Unethical behavior or unauthorized use of electronic devices during assessment will result in a failing grade (0.0).
bibliography: Jeff Hecht, UNDERSTANDING LASERS: AN ENTRY-LEVEL GUIDE , IEEE, 2008
W.Steen, J. Mazumder, LASER MATERIALS PROCESSING , Springer, 2010
